description: Ability to lead and deploy enterprise digital platforms for strategic needs identification and planning.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.'
change to work: Strategy formation must now include establishing and maintaining digital needs identification tools, actively leveraging organizational business intelligence, and embedding automation/AI-driven triage early in program strategy.
justification: Shift from manual/expert-driven need identification to technology-driven, enterprise-wide platforms introduces novel digital platform selection, management, and integration requirements.

description: Expertise in using business intelligence systems for data-driven strategic decision making, particularly in needs assessment and prioritization.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.'
change to work: Strategy formation must now include establishing and maintaining digital needs identification tools, actively leveraging organizational business intelligence, and embedding automation/AI-driven triage early in program strategy.
justification: Core to future planning is an understanding and application of business intelligence tools for strategic automation and resource evaluation.

description: Capacity to evaluate, select, and integrate automated triage or process solutions, minimizing manual or survey-based processes.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.'
change to work: System/process implementation must prioritize automation, digital solution reuse, and cost/resource triage before new data collection. Chiefs will direct teams away from surveys by default toward automation-first solutions.
justification: Implementing automated triage tools and workflows requires new skills and knowledge beyond traditional survey or system rollout.

description: In-depth knowledge of digital triage processes and tools for automating the justification of new or modified statistical programs.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - 'Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies, proposes innovative solutions and recommends to senior officials of Statistics Canada new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.'
change to work: Strategic direction-setting now incorporates automated analysis of needs, risk/resource/cost calculus via digital tools, and requires leading justification frameworks that advance automation and reuse before new studies/surveys.
justification: Digitally-enabled cost-benefit/resource assessment and triage methods require knowledge of relevant tools, frameworks, and approaches.

description: Ability to create, maintain, and leverage inventories of internal and external data assets; knowledge of best-practices in data stewardship and governance frameworks.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - 'Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources...'
change to work: Initiation and implementation of solutions must prioritize enterprise data asset inventorying, reuse of internal/external assets, and formal coordination/justification via digital platforms, before escalating to new collections or systems.
justification: The expanded role in managing data asset inventories demands new data governance and inventory management skills.

description: Leading, supporting, and managing teams through digital transformation and continuous upskilling in automation/data asset techniques.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 2. Leadership and operational management - 'Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.'
change to work: Team management must explicitly integrate digital skills, and Chiefs will need to lead upskilling initiatives, guide staff through automation transitions, and foster data asset-oriented operational culture.
justification: The team will lag without proactive digital/automation/asset management upskilling led by the Chief.

description: Understanding and applying digital platforms for cataloguing, reviewing, and reusing statistical assets to inform iterative strategic planning.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.'
change to work: This activity will be refocused toward continuous asset evaluation, leveraging existing data before considering new program development. Long-term strategies will be iterative, informed by platform-supported needs confirmation and transparent reuse analyses.
justification: Shift in strategy requires knowledge in digital asset catalogues and platform analysis for iterative planning.

description: Ability to critically evaluate statistical assets using automated platforms, including transparent documentation of reuse and outcomes.
historic work: Technical Activities: Decision making: 'Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.'
change to work: Decision making will prioritize reuse of existing/alternative data sources over the traditional initiation of new surveys; justification for new surveys is rigorous, requiring transparent platform-based asset reviews and cost-benefit analysis.
justification: Role must assess suitability of existing assets using automated consultation tools and catalogues.

description: Skill in articulating and documenting rigorous justification for new surveys, including cost-benefit and outcome analysis using digital tools.
historic work: Technical Activities: Decision making: 'Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.'
change to work: Decision making will prioritize reuse of existing/alternative data sources over the traditional initiation of new surveys; justification for new surveys is rigorous, requiring transparent platform-based asset reviews and cost-benefit analysis.
justification: Comprehensive justification and trade-off analysis for new surveys is necessary.

description: Skill in using digital tools to weight competing needs, integrate cross-functional input, and iteratively update research and development milestones.
historic work: Technical Activities: Decision making: 'Manages complex studies covering a range of departmental statistical programs, determines the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.'
change to work: More frequent use of iterative, platform-driven review of objectives, content, and methods. Prioritization will increasingly rely on evidence from existing data assets and rapid cross-departmental consultations, requiring integration of consultation tools.
justification: Prioritization and integration across programs demand platform-enabled decision support.

description: Ability to use consultation and asset platforms for efficient, transparent client engagement and needs-confirmation.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.'
change to work: Shift from deployment of new systems toward championing platform tools for transparent evaluation and consultation with clients. New methods and processes will focus on integration and optimization of reuse.
justification: Critical engagement with clients through digital consultation platforms requires new communication approaches.

description: Skill in negotiating resources and services using outcome-focused, platform-supported evidence and transparent asset evaluation.
historic work: Communication: 'Negotiates significant resources and services, timeframes and costs for large scale projects with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.'
change to work: Resource and timeframe negotiation will increasingly be informed by platform-based evidence and rigorous cost-benefit analysis. Focus shifts toward transparent communication on asset reuse, outcome justification, and efficiency.
justification: Negotiations will require new evidence and justification approaches.

description: Skill in supporting and managing evaluation programs across sectors using platform tools for interdepartmental collaboration and asset extension.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Plans, develops and manages a comprehensive program of detailed analysis and evaluation across sectors and departments to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the application of divisional statistics.'
change to work: Program management will prioritize extension and improvement of existing assets, supported by digital evaluation platforms and agile cross-departmental integration.
justification: Focus on cross-sector and digital integration demands new collaborative analytical skills.

description: Expertise in identifying, evaluating, and integrating automation solutions and digital workflows into statistical program strategies.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.'
change to work: Long-term strategies must now be developed and implemented with direct, up-front consideration of automation readiness, digital workflow compatibility, and asset reuse. Each proposed program must include a feasibility assessment for these parameters and explicit scoping for machine-actionable outputs.
justification: Chief must evaluate automation readiness and digital workflow compatibility as core to strategy formation, requiring advanced digital process and automation design knowledge.

development area: Cost/Benefit Analysis for Automation vs. Survey Approaches
description: Ability to conduct structured analyses on time, resource, and quality trade-offs between traditional survey methods and automated or digital alternatives.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.'
change to work: Long-term strategies must now be developed and implemented with direct, up-front consideration of automation readiness, digital workflow compatibility, and asset reuse. Each proposed program must include a feasibility assessment for these parameters and explicit scoping for machine-actionable outputs.
justification: Chief must formally justify all survey solutions, requiring advanced cost-benefit and trade-off evaluation skills, especially regarding digital and automation alternatives.

development area: Automation Frameworks and Digital Asset Evaluation
description: Advanced understanding of leading automation frameworks, asset reuse evaluation, and digital interoperability mechanisms, to inform objective-setting and recommendations.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Decision making - 'Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies...proposes innovative solutions and recommends...new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.'
change to work: Strategic direction now includes criteria for automation readiness, asset reuse, and digital workflow compatibility; recommendations must be justified with respect to these parameters before program approval.
justification: Chief must have knowledge of and be able to apply automation frameworks and digital asset evaluation methods, enabling innovative solutions that prioritize digital interoperability.

description: Ability to assess and ensure new systems, data sources, and technologies meet interoperability standards and support machine-actionable outputs.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Decision making - 'Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.'
change to work: Changing systems and processes must be justified based on digital compatibility and automation potential, and the Chief must evaluate new data sources and technology explicitly for their machine-actionability and interoperability.
justification: Chief needs to understand digital interoperability and machine-actionable output criteria, and assess new technologies for fit within digital-first data ecosystem.

description: Skill in creating and applying evaluation frameworks that measure automation readiness, digital compatibility, and asset reuse potential for statistical program methods and concepts.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Decision making - 'Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results...to extend the use of statistical programs.'
change to work: Review and evaluation now include explicit criteria for automation, reusability, and digital workflow integration at the program design and approval stages.
justification: Chief must develop and apply new evaluation criteria for digital and automation readiness, asset reuse, and workflow interoperability at both review and planning stages.

development area: Digital Change Management and Team Enablement
description: Ability to lead teams through digital and automation transitions, including training, knowledge transfer, and process change enablement to meet machine-actionability and interoperability requirements.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Leadership and operational management - 'Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.'
change to work: Leading multidisciplinary teams now includes responsibility to ensure teams can evaluate and document automation and digital workflow feasibility for each project, and that outputs are scoped for digital and machine-actionable requirements.
justification: Chief needs both leadership and hands-on technical skills to guide, mentor, and enable teams in automation and digital asset integration.

description: Ability to interpret, assess, and validate machine-generated statistical concepts/frameworks for program relevance.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > 'Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.'
change to work: Manual management and evaluation will shift to oversight of automated identification, with increased need for strategic arbitration of machine-driven results and exception handling. The Chief will focus on validating machine-generated frameworks and facilitating digital integration across teams.
justification: The transition from manual to machine-driven conceptualization and framework development requires familiarity with AI systems, digital integration, and metadata structures.

description: Skill to lead negotiation, establish digital integration frameworks, and arbitrate among machine-generated options and human priorities.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > 'Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.'
change to work: Manual management and evaluation will shift to oversight of automated identification, with increased need for strategic arbitration of machine-driven results and exception handling. The Chief will focus on validating machine-generated frameworks and facilitating digital integration across teams.
justification: Role requires guiding and arbitrating cross-team decisions and integrating digital assets.

description: Advanced understanding of metadata structures, standards for interoperability, and their programmatic application.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > 'Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.'
change to work: Manual management and evaluation will shift to oversight of automated identification, with increased need for strategic arbitration of machine-driven results and exception handling. The Chief will focus on validating machine-generated frameworks and facilitating digital integration across teams.
justification: Consistent and strategic management of metadata becomes foundational to interoperability.

description: Ability to validate exceptions in AI-driven statistical concepts and arbitrate strategic program decisions.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > 'Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results, to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, to ensure the continued relevancy of data in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions and to extend the use of statistical programs.'
change to work: Evaluation moves towards validating quality and completeness of AI-driven frameworks, with special emphasis on exception handling and strategic alignment across digital assets.
justification: Updating to system-guided identification requires new evaluative expertise in both digital systems and arbitration.

description: Capability to evaluate, select, and implement machine-driven and automated statistical processes.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > 'Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.'
change to work: Initiation of new systems/processes now must include evaluation of AI-driven methods, reliability of machine-guided frameworks, digital integration, and long-term program impact of automated processes.
justification: Changing systems and processes now needs understanding of digital transformation, automation impacts, and AI assessment.

description: Comprehensive knowledge of modern artificial intelligence methods applied to statistical conceptualization and framework development.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 4. Knowledge of specialized fields > 'Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.'
change to work: Expanded to include deep fluency in AI methods for statistical concept identification and digital frameworks.
justification: Expertise must span traditional statistical methods and modern AI-driven/statistical theory.

description: Skills to lead digital integration projects with cross-domain teams, leveraging AI systems and arbitration frameworks.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 4. Knowledge of specialized fields > 'Knowledge of management practices and the theories and principles of project management in order to manage staff, either directly or within a matrix management environment.'
change to work: Project management adapts to account for digital integration, oversight of multi-domain arbitration, and metadata-driven decision making.
justification: Managing teams and projects will require digital integration approaches and coordination with AI-guided systems.

description: Advanced understanding of how metadata-driven platforms work and how to strategically leverage automation for statistical program development.
historic work: Key Activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.
change to work: Strategy development now centers on integrating and leveraging metadata-enabled automated platforms. The Chief must adapt strategies to optimize and validate these new systems and processes.
justification: Automation systems require leaders to envision strategic adoption and optimization of metadata and automation; foundational knowledge is lacking in current description.

description: Ability to understand, interpret, and validate the outputs and functioning of automated, metadata-driven decision systems.
historic work: Key Activities: Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.
change to work: Chiefs now implement, validate, and maintain automated decision logic and meta-driven systems, and must assess their legal, cost, and ethical implications, shifting focus to process oversight rather than manual evaluation.
justification: Transition from manual process management to oversight of automated system outputs and cost/efficiency evaluations requires additional system-logic knowledge.

description: Skill in interpreting, contextualizing, and acting upon complex outputs from automated and metadata-driven suitability screening tools and platforms.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts: Decision making: Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.
change to work: The Chief's decision-making is increasingly based on the outputs of automated systems, and they must interpret, validate, and strategically deploy these results, as well as resolve complex legal/ethical risks and partnership challenges resulting from automated findings.
justification: Chiefs must now interpret automated suitability and source evaluation, requiring technical skills in platform logic and risk management—these capacities are not explicit in the current description.

change to work: The Chief's decision-making is increasingly based on the outputs of automated systems, and they must interpret, validate, and strategically deploy these results, as well as resolve complex legal/ethical risks and partnership challenges resulting from automated findings.
